eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: State creation gas cost increase cited as the reason the gas limit needs to reach at least 150M at the Glamsterdam fork.

moments.context: Maria explained that 8037's cost-per-state-byte increase means some transactions require much more gas, making a gas limit below 150M problematic.
Helkomine noted that 8037 would massively drive up deployment costs without a discount like SETCODEFROM or 8058.

eips.title: Limit and meter initcode
eips.summary: Referenced as the initcode pricing EIP that should have already addressed the JUMPDEST analysis attack vector.

moments.context: Jochem noted the attack involves CREATE initcode and should have been fixed by EIP-3860's 2 gas/word pricing.

eips.title: Gas Limit Schedule
eips.summary: Jochem linked Barnabas's gas limit schedule EIP in chat during the gas limit discussion.

moments.context: Jochem shared the link to EIP-8261 in chat when discussing whether a gas limit schedule mechanism exists.

eips.title: Increase exit and consolidation churn
eips.summary: Increase exit and consolidation churn was discussed as the cause of the CL block retention window needing adjustment.

moments.context: danceratopz explained that 8061 changed a key CL parameter but the block retention window was not updated to reflect it.
Kev asked whether the CL window should be reduced according to 8061, which would roughly halve it.
Kev noted the current 33k epoch window could be reduced to about 2 months if adjusted per 8061.

eips.title: Reduce CL Block Retention Window
eips.summary: Referenced as a Hegota PFI EIP that would further reduce the CL block retention window.

moments.context: danceratopz mentioned EIP-8383 as a related Hegota PFI that reduces the CL block retention window further.

eips.title: Bound Historical Data in Execution Clients
eips.summary: Kev noted that EIP-4444's history bound was changed to 33,024 epochs to match the CL retention window.

moments.context: Kev said EIP-4444 was changed to 33,024 to match the CL retention window, and reducing the CL window per 8061 would roughly halve it.

eips.title: Independent CL/EL Sync
eips.summary: Potuz repeatedly noted that independent CL/EL sync would have made the BAL retention discussion moot.

moments.context: Potuz said they should not have DFI'd 8237 because it would make all BAL and payload retention questions irrelevant.

eips.title: Trustless log and transaction index
eips.summary: Trustless log and transaction index was DFI'd for Hegota after Besu and Reth confirmed no change in their positions.

moments.context: nixo raised 8304 as a DFI candidate from the previous call, asking Besu and Reth if they had adjusted their recommendations.
Zsolt said he would continue working on the project regardless of the DFI decision and invited interested parties to reach out.

eips.title: Call and Return Opcodes for the EVM
eips.summary: Call and return opcodes for the EVM received broad client support and was moved to CFI for Hegota.

moments.context: Greg Colvin summarized performance measurements and end-to-end testing with Solidity showing all tests pass with the new opcodes.
Solidity representative confirmed they would implement it when delivered and shared their opinion in the ETH Magicians thread.
Dragan confirmed Reth support, noting their SOLAR compiler team would like to use it, upgrading from a C.
Ben Adams from Nethermind strongly supported it, saying it has been considered a good idea for nine years and should ship now.
Besu said Solidity's support changed their opinion and they are open to moving it from B to A.
nixo proposed moving 7979 to CFI with no strong opposition; multiple clients confirmed support in chat.

eips.title: Foundations of EVM Control Flow
eips.summary: Greg Colvin referenced it as the foundations of EVM control flow document linked from the 7979 proposal.

moments.context: Greg mentioned 8173 on foundations of control flow as background reading for understanding the 7979 proposal.

eips.title: Validated EVM Code
eips.summary: Referenced by Greg Colvin as a validated EVM code proposal that is a natural follow-up to 7979.

moments.context: Greg described 8337 as a proposal for showing code is valid with five criteria, and Solidity said they would be more in favor if it followed 7979.

eips.title: Simple Subroutines for the EVM
eips.summary: Greg noted that Charles from Vyper prefers 2315 over 7979 but would still use the new opcodes.

moments.context: Greg relayed that Charles would say he likes 2315 better but would definitely use the 7979 opcodes.

eips.title: Reserve `EXTENSION (0xae)` opcode
eips.summary: Reserve EXTENSION opcode was moved to CFI after L2 demand evidence and client support as a trivial no-op on L1.

moments.context: nixo raised 8163 as a DFI candidate and asked for L2/EVM chain feedback.
Piotr from Mononaut Foundation presented evidence of demand from Tron, Rootstock, and Arbitrum Nitro.
Besu promoted it to S tier, Erigon to B, Reth said C or B, ethrex said C. No opposition; moved to CFI.

eips.title: TCREATE Opcode
eips.summary: TCREATE opcode was discussed as covering ephemeral contract use cases but not decided; deferred to next call.

moments.context: Milos presented TCREATE for disposable contracts, arguing Glamsterdam's refund removal effectively breaks this use case.
Jochem argued the EVM is effectively deprecating this feature without an alternative and should schedule one for Hegota.
Ben Adams said some use cases could be covered by SETCODEFROM but not all, and TCREATE would let them fully remove self-destruct.
Maria said the discussion should be coupled with the self-destruct deprecation decision; nixo deferred to next call.

eips.title: Block-Level Access Lists
eips.summary: Block-level access lists noted as already included when checking TCREATE dependencies.

moments.context: nixo checked TCREATE's dependencies and noted 7928 is already included.

eips.title: Transient storage opcodes
eips.summary: Referenced as already part of the chain when explaining that TCREATE's SSTORE/SLOAD behaves like TSTORE/TLOAD.

moments.context: Jochem clarified that SSTORE behaves as TSTORE in TCREATE contracts, referencing EIP-1153 as already deployed.

eips.title: CPSB Recalibration for New Gas Limit
eips.summary: CPSB recalibration left in PFI along with 8372 pending mainnet data after Glamsterdam.

moments.context: nixo noted both 8368 and 8372 need at least 30 days of mainnet data post-Glamsterdam before a decision; left as PFI.

eips.title: Normalized state gas limit
eips.summary: Normalized state gas limit left in PFI alongside 8368 pending post-Glamsterdam mainnet data.

moments.context: nixo proposed leaving both 8368 and 8372 in PFI since neither can be decided until mainnet data is available.

eips.title: Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
eips.summary: Transaction assertions via state diff opcode was the highest rated PFI and moved to CFI with no opposition.

moments.context: nixo presented 7906 as the highest rated EIP and asked for concerns; Suyash from Firmware strongly recommended it for hardware signers.
No opposition raised; moved to CFI.

eips.title: Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions
eips.summary: Keyed nonces for frame transactions moved to CFI with no concerns raised.

moments.context: nixo asked for concerns on 8250; none raised, moved to CFI as part of the account abstraction batch.

eips.title: Recent Roots for Frame Transactions
eips.summary: Recent roots for frame transactions moved to CFI alongside 8250 as a frame transactions bundle.

moments.context: nixo grouped 8272 with 8250 as frame transaction EIPs and moved it to CFI with no opposition.

eips.title: Remove bloom filters
eips.summary: Remove bloom filters moved to CFI; Ben Adams noted they are computed and sent but nobody uses them.

moments.context: nixo raised 7668 noting it has been proposed for three forks; Ben Adams called it technical debt removal since nobody uses bloom filters.

eips.title: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
eips.summary: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts moved to CFI as the replacement for EIP-7610.

moments.context: Jochem explained 8253 is the EIP-7610 replacement that was SFI'd then last-minute DFI'd for Glamsterdam; moved to CFI.

eips.title: Revert creation in case of non-empty storage
eips.summary: Referenced as the EIP that 8253 replaces after being DFI'd last minute from Glamsterdam.

moments.context: Jochem stated 8253 is the EIP-7610 replacement, noting 7610 was SFI'd for Glamsterdam then DFI'd at the last minute.

eips.title: Remove storage-clear refund and refund cap
eips.summary: Remove storage-clear refund and refund cap moved to CFI despite lower priority ratings from Erigon and ethrex.

moments.context: nixo asked about the lower tier ratings from Erigon and ethrex; Andrew from Erigon said it was just lower priority, no specific concern. Moved to CFI.

eips.title: Unified Transaction Content Floor
eips.summary: Unified transaction content floor moved to CFI with all client ratings at A or B and no concerns.

moments.context: nixo presented 8131 as the last easy CFI; all ratings were A or B with no flags raised.
Ansgar and Toni argued 8131 should be bundled with the block access list byte floor (8279), since doing only one leaves the worst-case block size unchanged.

eips.title: SETCODEFROM Code Reuse Instruction
eips.summary: SETCODEFROM code reuse instruction discussed for CFI; Besu asked for more time, deferred to next call.

moments.context: Lightclient said SETCODEFROM is important; CPerezz shared a walkthrough article and offered to help client teams.
CPerezz explained how SETCODEFROM enables migration from EOA to smart accounts and post-quantum readiness.

Dragan explained Reth's DFI was not a strong opinion, just wanting to delay code-change decisions until after frames. Nico argued timing risks with post-quantum concerns make Hegota inclusion important.
Besu said they find arguments compelling but need more time; nixo deferred the decision to next call.

eips.title: Block Access List Byte Floor
eips.summary: Raised as the bundle partner to 8131 for unified data pricing; clients were not asked to decide on the call.

moments.context: Ansgar named the block access list byte floor as the other data-pricing EIP and said it and 8131 go hand-in-hand toward a more unified approach to data pricing, adding it was only a suggestion and that clients not ready to decide today was fine.
Toni agreed the two should be seen as a bundle, because doing only one of them leaves the worst-case block size unchanged.

eips.title: Contract Bytecode Deduplication Discount
eips.summary: Contract bytecode deduplication discount mentioned as related to but superseded by SETCODEFROM.

moments.context: Helkomine and CPerezz discussed 8058; CPerezz said SETCODEFROM is a superset of 8058 and he is the author of both.
Helkomine argued that 8058 and 8298 should be able to coexist since Uniswap factory sub-contracts have identical code.

eips.title: Account Code Restricted ecRecover
eips.summary: Account code restricted ecRecover was mentioned as related to SETCODEFROM but had no discussion or decision.

moments.context: Nico asked if 8151 was discussed; nixo confirmed no discussion or decision on it today.

eips.title: Set Code for EOAs
eips.summary: Referenced in SETCODEFROM discussion as the alternative for users who want to keep EOA functionality.

moments.context: CPerezz explained that SETCODEFROM migrates to a full code account while 7702 keeps EOA natively for those who don't want to fully migrate.
